transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Garcia (SummitPay Eng Lead), Priyanka Rao (SummitPay DevOps), Samir Khan (SummitPay CTO)
Recording: yes

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Went through SDK quickstarts for python and typescript, showed env var set up, auth options, console keys, and recommended optimize settings. Customer asked about SAML SSO, private deployment options and latency numbers for dedicated. Next: send docs and sandbox key, start pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you carving out time. I'm Jordan Ellis, AE at Redwood. With me is Priya Patel our platform SE.
[00:07] Priya: Hi everyone. I'll be doing the bulk of the SDK walkthrough and quickstarts.
[00:12] Alex: Thanks, Jordan. Samir, Priyanka and I are here. We're excited to see the integration flow, particularly for Python and TS since that's what our teams use.
[00:18] Jordan: Perfect. High level agenda - quick intros, Priya will jump into the SDK quickstarts, auth flows, then console and optimize tips, and we'll leave time for Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[00:26] Priyanka: Yep, that works.
[00:29] Priya: Alright jumping in. I'm sharing my screen, should be a browser + VSCode. Let me know if you don't see it.
[00:35] Alex: We can see it.
[00:37] Priya: Cool. So first the Python quickstart: pip install redwood-sdk, set your REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var, then a simple call to redwood.Client().generate. Here's an example.
[00:50] Speaker 1: "from redwood import Redwood, Response" look, this is - sorry transcription note, sometimes the package name was captured odd.
[00:58] Priya: Right, sometimes the pip package is transcribed as rewood or something. The canonical is redwood-inference-sdk for pip and @redwood/inference for npm.
[01:08] Alex: Quick question - how do you recommend storing keys? We have vault + KMS in prod.
[01:12] Priya: Great Q. For prod we recommend platform KMS + environment secrets or Hashi Vault. For hosted API you can use scoped API keys from the Console and rotate them; for Private deployments we do KMS integrates with customer HSMs.
[01:25] Priyanka: Are there examples for SSO? We use Okta and want SAML-based SSO for the control plane.
[01:30] Jordan: Yes, we support SAML/SSO for the Console and RBAC. I'll share the SAML pack. I'll also attach SOC 2 and ISO docs.
[01:37] Priya: Back to the quickstart - here's a simple snippet in Python that will stream responses, and here's how to enable streaming in TypeScript too.
[01:47] Priya: (shows code) Example env: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-sandbox-xxxx; REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood.ai/v1; then run python quickstart.py
[01:58] Alex: Ok good. What's the sandbox rate limits? We're going to run some small perf tests.
[02:03] Jordan: Sandbox keys are low-rate by default, we can open a temp higher rate for benchmark runs - Priya will coordinate.
[02:11] Priya: For perf runs we usually recommend a short dedicated pilot so you can validate steady-state latency with batching. If you want to run raw SDK tests we can provide a short-lived key with bumped qps.
[02:21] Alex: Nice. Can you show the TS quickstart?
[02:24] Priya: Sure - switching to the TypeScript tab. npm i @redwood/inference, then .env with REDWOOD_API_KEY. Example code: import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-13b', messages: [...] });
[02:42] Samir: We use node lambdas for a lot of small inference calls - any latency guidance?
[02:48] Priya: Two parts - network and model. For hosted API you'll see median p95 around X to Y ms for small models - note: the exact numbers vary by model size and region. For strict SLAs we recommend Dedicated pools which give predictable throughput; we can share sample latency numbers from similar customers. Also note automatic prefix/KV 'KV cash' caching can reduce token cost and latency.
[03:12] Priyanka: Did you say KV cash? (laughs)
[03:15] Priya: I meant KV cache - sorry the transcript is messy.
[03:18] Alex: On dedicated, we need SOC2 and audit logs and ability to pin model versions - does Redwood support that?
[03:24] Jordan: Yes to all - Dedicated includes pinning, longer logs retention options as an add-on, and full audit trails. We'll include the SOC2 PDF and examples of audit log entries.
[03:33] Priya: Now console quick demo - I'm opening the Console. Top right is the API Keys page where you can create scoped keys, set TTL, and restrict routes. Over here is the model catalog and per-model perf stats.
[03:46] Priya: If you go to Routes -> Create Route, you can map an API route to a model + rollout policy - very handy for canaries. I'll create a route for our python quickstart demo.
[03:58] Alex: Can we restrict keys per-environment? We run staging and prod separate.
[04:02] Priya: Yep, create keys per workspace or per route, and you can tie them to roles. For SSO we map Okta groups to RBAC.
[04:10] Samir: Any way to see token-level cost on the Console? Our finance team asks for per-feature cost.
[04:15] Jordan: Console has token breakdowns and per-route cost analytics. It shows per-invocation tokens, batching efficiency, and a projected monthly spend.
[04:24] Priya: Now quick note on Optimize - if you have many short requests we recommend batching windows and prefix caching. Also quantization profiles can reduce GPU memory and cost. We'll suggest a model and quant profile after seeing your sample workload.
[04:38] Alex: That sounds good. For the quickstarts, will you share a sample docker-compose env for local testing? Our devs like that pattern.
[04:45] Priya: Yes, quickstarts include docker-compose with env var examples and a sample mock server to emulate the Console callback endpoints. I'll put that in the repo link.
[04:53] Priyanka: One more security Q: data retention for logs? We need 7 years retention for audit logs for compliance.
[04:59] Jordan: That's long, but for Private deployments and Dedicated with enterprise add-ons we support extended retention or can push logs to your SIEM via our log-forwarding integration. We'll follow up with specifics.
[05:10] Alex: Great. Can you show a short end-to-end example? From code to Console to seeing logs?
[05:15] Priya: Sure - I'll run the python quickstart which hits the sandbox key; then flip to Console logs and you'll see the request, token usage and latency. Running now...
[05:26] (demo running, some typing noise)
[05:34] Priya: Request completed, popping into Logs -> Requests... you can see request id, route, model, tokens in and out. The trace links to cold-starts or kernel selection if applicable.
[05:45] Alex: That trace looks helpful. If we host on VPC or on-prem, do we still get these traces?
[05:52] Priya: For Private deployments we offer a control plane that can either send anonymized metrics to Redwood or you can keep everything on-prem and integrate with your observability. We also support a log-forwarder to your ELK/Datadog.
[06:05] Samir: Latency for on-prem versus hosted - I assume on-prem depends entirely on our infra. Any tooling to benchmark?
[06:12] Priya: We provide benchmarking harnesses that you can run against the runtime; we'll include those scripts in the repo to collect p50/p95/p99 and memory profiles.
[06:21] Alex: For the TypeScript example, do you support both REST and SDK wrappers? We sometimes go REST to avoid additional deps.
[06:28] Priya: Yes both. The SDK wraps the REST calls and adds streaming helpers, retry/backoff and automatic token refresh for SSO flows. If you prefer REST that's fully supported - examples for curl and fetch are in the quickstarts.
[06:40] Priyanka: Do you have examples of batching in the node sdk for lambda usage?
[06:44] Priya: We have a small batching library example that you can drop into node lambdas. It shows a micro-batcher that collects requests for up to X ms or Y requests before dispatch. We'll attach that.
[06:55] Alex: About pricing - are there volume discounts for dedicated pools?
[06:59] Jordan: Yes dedicated is typically commit-based monthly or annual with discounts based on utilization. We'll send the template pricing and a couple of configurations that match your traffic profile.
[07:10] (brief pause)
[07:12] Priya: Quick gotcha on env: make sure you don't commit REDWOOD_API_KEY in repos, use secrets manager and gitignore .env. Common mistake we see.
[07:21] Alex: Yep agreed.
[07:23] Speaker 2: small crosstalk, someone saying 'we'll have an internal RFC'
[07:28] Priya: Ok I'm going to share the repo link in chat: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (note: example link may be mocked). It contains python/, typescript/, docker/, and bench/ folders.
[07:40] Alex: Got it. Thanks.
[07:42] Priyanka: For SSO, Jordan mentioned RBAC - how are roles mapped?
[07:47] Jordan: In the Console you map Okta groups to Redwood roles (Admin, Dev, Observer). You can restrict route creation to Admins and give read-only to Observers.
[07:57] Samir: Any compliance for payments industry - PCI scope?
[08:02] Jordan: We don't store raw card numbers by design and recommend tokenization on your side before sending. For higher compliance needs we can discuss Private deployments and the scope of what Redwood processes. We'll put that in the security doc.
[08:15] Alex: For the pilot, what do you need from us to size the dedicated pool?
[08:20] Priya: Send us 1) a representative traffic trace (requests/sec, token distribution), 2) desired latency p95 targets, 3) peak concurrency. We'll then recommend a config and expected cost.
[08:32] Alex: We'll pull that together.
[08:34] Priya: Two small demo follow-ups: 1) I'll attach an example envrc and docker-compose; 2) I'll include a short script to run synthetic load.
[08:43] Jordan: Next steps recap - I'll send SAML + SOC2 + pricing, Priya will share quickstart repo and sandbox key, and Alex will send traffic profile. Does that capture it?
[08:55] Alex: Yes that works.
[08:57] Samir: Sounds good.
[09:00] Priyanka: One more question - how does rollback/rollout work if we do canary?
[09:05] Priya: Routes support canary rollouts where a percent of traffic goes to new model; you can set automatic fallback to prior model on error rate. We'll demo that in the next call if you want.
[09:16] (silence for a bit, some side chatter)
[09:25] Jordan: Ok, if no more questions we can wrap. Thanks for your time, we'll follow up with the pack.
[09:30] Alex: Appreciate it.
[09:32] Priya: Thanks all.

End of meeting notes: Action items and links will be posted in CRM and shared via email.
